topic: Selected-platform deletion after original crew object deletion
finding: The existing native platform Deleted callback refused any null original crew member. A corpse removed before the platform therefore left the selected reference reserved even though that original movement actor no longer existed. The prior watcher did not preserve private original-actor provenance.
implementation: Capture a private copy of both typed nonnull original crew references when installing the existing handler. A repeat installation keeps its original snapshot and refuses a changed crew journal.

At the genuine native platform-deletion callback require the exact work reference/group/owner and private crew snapshot. Each original must be deleted or local and dead. Living originals, remote existing actors, missing initial objects and replaced journals refuse.

Retain exact original lease cleanup and protection of newer/unknown public and private reservations. Publish GONE when an original object was deleted; retain DEAD for two present dead originals. Tactical operation termination remains INCOMPLETE.
Group locality-loss cleanup recognises the extended private watcher shape. No cross-owner reconstruction from already-missing actors.

nativeSemantics.finding: Actual deletion turns an object reference into objNull on the next frame. This supports retaining original references before disappearance; it does not prove event ordering or MP behaviour in CBE.

sourceIntent: Preserve finite selected-platform crew scope and original group membership; no source relocation loop, teleport, crew replacement or new controller is copied. Historical selected source comparison remains in artillery-casualty-retirement-gap-20261025.json and armour-selected-standoff-20261025.json.
cost: Copy two object references once per admitted watcher installation. Existing one local Deleted handler and fixed two-actor event checks; no additional listener, scan, timer or recurring callback. Runtime overhead unmeasured.
limits: Living original crew, split actor ownership, a missing initial capture, already-missing actors on a new owner and absent genuine platform deletion still refuse.
Does not certify foreign live-worker termination or general native supersession.
Native event ordering, repeated use, normal/HC migration and performance budget remain unverified. Audits paused.
